summary: Dedicated pool throughput sag in us-west: background IO surge causing GPU attach latency and tenant throttling
description:
Issue summary:
During the late-afternoon window on 2026-03-10 we observed a sustained drop in throughput for a reserved dedicated pool in us-west-2 serving NimbleDocs (dedicated). Symptoms included elevated attach/slot acquisition latency, increased 429s on batched routes, and an observed decline in concurrent GPU allocations for the affected pool.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: ~12% increase in end-to-end p95 latency for their batched text generation routes between 14:10-15:05 PST; intermittent 429s and throttled requests.
- Platform: allocator reported temporary reduction of available attachable slots; autoscaler did not spawn new nodes due to perceived low utilization.

Environment:
- Prod, us-west-2, dedicated pool id: rp-2831 (NimbleDocs reserved cluster).
- Serving runtime: 1.8.3-release
- Allocator: v0.22.1
- Snapshotter-sidecar: v0.9.6

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start sustained small-stream workload (many short streaming sessions) against customer's pinned model.
2) At ~14:00, background snapshot flush job (system task) triggered high NVMe/io-write on a subset of hosts in the reserved cluster.
3) Shortly after, attach latency p95 jumps and new session attaches start failing with timeouts; queued requests build up and autoscaler does not react as expected.

Observed behavior and telemetry: 
- attach_latency_p95 for cluster rp-2831 rose from ~18ms baseline to ~320ms within 4 minutes.
- gpu_attach_failures increased and correlated with nvme_write_latency spikes on 6/24 hosts in the pool.
- autoscaler metrics showed allocation_decision_rate steady but available_slots metric dropped; allocation decisions aborted due to sidecar attach hang.
- Sidecar logs include repeated errors: "snapshotter: flush delay > 120s, initiating write-back" and socket-level write timeouts.

Initial hypotheses:
- Snapshotter-sidecar flush induced NVMe IO pressure causing host-level stalls that prolong attach handshake (noisy sidecar).
- Small-stream heavy fanout from tenant amplifies the attach overload and causes queue serialization on allocator.
- Autoscaler logic misinterpreted temporary attach stalls as low demand, delaying scale-up.

Investigation notes: 
- Collected dmesg and nvme SMART logs from affected hosts (links in comments).
- Confirmed that background maintenance job launched by orchestration-runner at 14:05 produced concurrent GC/flush on reserved hosts.
- Heap profile from snapshotter shows a large flush batch size change pushed in last config rollout (PR referenced below).
- Kernel stack samples show context-switch stalls during nvme write spikes.

Workarounds applied to mitigate customer impact: 
- Support routed small percentage (~10%) of traffic to fallback region eu-west temporarily for high-concurrency routes to reduce pressure.
- RPM: throttled snapshotter-sidecar flush interval on affected hosts to reduce IO concurrency.
- Applied transient throttling on batch concurrency for the NimbleDocs routes from the console to reduce attach churn.

Next steps / Action items: 
- Engineering (allocator + runtime) to add backoff for attach retries so autoscaler distinguishes between attach stall and low demand (owner: Ravi).
- Snapshotter team to revert the recent aggressive flush batching change or gate it behind host IO checks (owner: Maria Lopez).
- SRE to add NVMe write-latency alerting tied to allocator decisions to trigger automatic routing to alternate pools.
- Postmortem and runbook update: include "snapshot-flush" as a noisy-neighbor vector and mitigation checklist.

Resolution notes (so far):
- Immediate customer impact reduced after snapshotter throttle and traffic re-routing. Root cause still being validated across full fleet.
- A temporary patch was rolled to decrease flush concurrency on us-west-2 reserved hosts; full revert or safe rollout planned after verification.

Relevant artifacts and links referenced during investigation are in comments below.
